title: एकविंशतितमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Duryodhana, in his chariot, fights bravely and cannot be borne by the Pandavas, wounding many and cutting their bows. Dhrishtadyumna and Duryodhana meet in a fierce duel, and the bamboo-grove roar of arrows rises.
summary.kn: ರಥದಲ್ಲಿ ದುರ್ಯೋಧನ ಧೈರ್ಯದಿಂದ ಹೋರಾಡಿ ಪಾಂಡವರಿಗೆ ಸಹಿಸಲಾಗದವನಾಗುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಅನೇಕರನ್ನು ಗಾಯಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಬಿಲ್ಲು ಕಡಿಯುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಧೃಷ್ಟದ್ಯುಮ್ನ-ದುರ್ಯೋಧನರ ಉಗ್ರ ದ್ವಂದ್ವ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ; ಬಾಣಗಳ ಘೋಷ ಬಿದಿರು ವನದ ಬೆಂಕಿಯಂತೆ ಏಳುತ್ತದೆ.
summary.hi: रथ में दुर्योधन साहस से लड़ता है और पाण्डवों के लिए असहनीय हो जाता है, बहुतों को घायल करता और धनुष काटता है। धृष्टद्युम्न और दुर्योधन का भीषण द्वन्द्व होता है और बाणों की ध्वनि बाँस-वन में आग जैसी उठती है।
summary.te: రథంలో దుర్యోధనుడు ధైర్యంగా పోరాడి పాండవులకు సహించరానివాడవుతాడు, అనేకులను గాయపరచి విల్లులు నరుకుతాడు. ధృష్టద్యుమ్న దుర్యోధనుల భీకర ద్వంద్వం జరుగుతుంది; బాణాల ధ్వని వెదురు వనంలో మంటలా లేస్తుంది.
summary.ta: தேரில் துரியோதனன் வீரமாகப் போரிட்டுப் பாண்டவருக்குத் தாங்க முடியாதவனாகி, பலரைக் காயப்படுத்தி வில்களை வெட்டுகிறான். த்ருஷ்டத்யும்னனும் துரியோதனனும் கடும் தனிப்போர் புரிய, அம்புகளின் ஒலி மூங்கில் காட்டில் தீ போல் எழுகிறது.
summary.ml: ദുര്യോധനൻ തന്റെ രഥത്തിൽ ധീരമായി പൊരുതുന്നു; പാണ്ഡവർക്ക് അദ്ദേഹത്തെ താങ്ങാനാകുന്നില്ല, പലരെയും മുറിവേൽപ്പിക്കുകയും അവരുടെ വില്ലുകൾ മുറിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു. ധൃഷ്ടദ്യുമ്നനും ദുര്യോധനനും കടുത്ത ദ്വന്ദ്വയുദ്ധത്തിൽ ഏർപ്പെടുന്നു; മുളങ്കാട്ടിലെന്നപോലെ അമ്പുകളുടെ ഇരമ്പൽ ഉയരുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 9.21; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Tue Jun 23 2020

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
पुत्रस्तु ते महाराज रथस्थो रथिनां वरः ।
दुरुत्सहो बभौ युद्धे यथा रुद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥

meaning.en: Your son, O great king, standing in his chariot, the best of chariot-fighters, shone in battle, hard to withstand, like blazing Rudra.

verses.text:
तस्य बाणसहस्रैस्तु प्रच्छन्ना ह्यभवन्मही ।
परांश्च सिषिचे बाणैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतान् ॥

meaning.en: The earth was covered with thousands of his arrows, and he drenched his enemies with shafts as rain streams on mountains.

verses.text:
न च सोऽस्ति पुमान्कश्चित्पाण्डवानां महाहवे ।
हयो गजो रथो वापि योऽस्य बाणैरविक्षतः ॥

meaning.en: In that great battle there was no man, horse, elephant or chariot of the Pandavas that his arrows had not wounded.

verses.text:
यं यं हि समरे योधं प्रपश्यामि विशां पते ।
स स बाणैश्चितोऽभूद्वै पुत्रेण तव भारत ॥

meaning.en: Whatever warrior I looked at in the battle, O lord of the people, O Bharata, was studded with your son's arrows.

verses.text:
यथा सैन्येन रजसा समुद्धूतेन वाहिनी ।
प्रत्यदृश्यत संछन्ना तथा बाणैर्महात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: As an army appears veiled by the dust its own troops raise, so it appeared covered by the arrows of that great-souled man.

verses.text:
बाणभूतामपश्याम पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते ।
दुर्योधनेन प्रकृतां क्षिप्रहस्तेन धन्विना ॥

meaning.en: We saw the earth turned to arrows, O lord of the earth, made so by Duryodhana, the quick-handed archer.

verses.text:
तेषु योधसहस्रेषु तावकेषु परेषु च ।
एको दुर्योधनो ह्यासीत्पुमानिति मतिर्मम ॥

meaning.en: Among those thousands of warriors, on your side and the enemy's, I thought Duryodhana alone was the true man.

verses.text:
तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव पुत्रस्य विक्रमम् ।
यदेकं सहिताः पार्था नात्यवर्तन्त भारत ॥

meaning.en: There we saw a marvel in your son's valor, O Bharata: the Parthas, though united, could not get past him alone.

verses.text:
युधिष्ठिरं शतेनाजौ विव्याध भरतर्षभ ।
भीमसेनं च सप्तत्या सहदेवं च सप्तभिः ॥

meaning.en: In the battle, O bull of the Bharatas, he pierced Yudhishthira with a hundred arrows, Bhimasena with seventy and Sahadeva with seven.

verses.text:
नकुलं च चतुःषष्ट्या धृष्टद्युम्नं च पञ्चभिः ।
सप्तभिर्द्रौपदेयांश्च त्रिभिर्विव्याध सात्यकिम् ।
धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन सहदेवस्य मारिष ॥

meaning.en: He pierced Nakula with sixty-four and Dhrishtadyumna with five, the sons of Draupadi with seven, and Satyaki with three, and with a broad-headed arrow he cut Sahadeva's bow, O revered one.

verses.text:
तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं माद्रीपुत्रः प्रतापवान् ।
अभ्यधावत राजानं प्रगृह्यान्यन्महद्धनुः ।
ततो दुर्योधनं संख्ये विव्याध दशभिः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: Casting aside the cut bow, the mighty son of Madri took another great bow and rushed at the king; then in the battle he pierced Duryodhana with ten arrows.

verses.text:
नकुलश्च ततो वीरो राजानं नवभिः शरैः ।
घोररूपैर्महेष्वासो विव्याध च ननाद च ॥

meaning.en: Then the hero Nakula, a great archer, pierced the king with nine dreadful arrows and roared.

verses.text:
सात्यकिश्चापि राजानं शरेणानतपर्वणा ।
द्रौपदेयास्त्रिसप्तत्या धर्मराजश्च सप्तभिः ।
अशीत्या भीमसेनश्च शरै राजानमार्दयत् ॥

meaning.en: Satyaki too struck the king with a straight-jointed arrow; the sons of Draupadi with seventy-three, King Dharmaraja with seven, and Bhimasena with eighty arrows, tormenting him.

verses.text:
समन्तात्कीर्यमाणस्तु बाणसंघैर्महात्मभिः ।
न चचाल महाराज सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: Though showered on every side by the great warriors' volleys of arrows, O great king, he did not waver, while the whole army watched.

verses.text:
लाघवं सौष्ठवं चापि वीर्यं चैव महात्मनः ।
अति सर्वाणि भूतानि ददृशुः सर्वमानवाः ॥

meaning.en: All men saw the great-souled king's lightness of hand, skill and valor surpass all other beings.

verses.text:
धार्तराष्ट्रास्तु राजेन्द्र यात्वा तु स्वल्पमन्तरम् ।
अपश्यमाना राजानं पर्यवर्तन्त दंशिताः ॥

meaning.en: The Dhartarashtras, O king of kings, had gone a little way, but not seeing their king, they turned back, armored again.

verses.text:
तेषामापततां घोरस्तुमुलः समजायत ।
क्षुब्धस्य हि समुद्रस्य प्रावृट्काले यथा निशि ॥

meaning.en: As they returned, a terrible tumult arose, like that of the stirred ocean on a rainy-season night.

verses.text:
समासाद्य रणे ते तु राजानमपराजितम् ।
प्रत्युद्ययुर्महेष्वासाः पाण्डवानाततायिनः ॥

meaning.en: Reaching the undefeated king in the battle, those great archers advanced against the Pandavas, their deadly foes.

verses.text:
भीमसेनं रणे क्रुद्धं द्रोणपुत्रो न्यवारयत् ।
ततो बाणैर्महाराज प्रमुक्तैः सर्वतोदिशम् ।
नाज्ञायन्त रणे वीरा न दिशः प्रदिशस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Ashvatthama, son of Drona, held back Bhimasena, angry in the battle. Then, O great king, with arrows loosed in every direction, the warriors could not tell the quarters or the intermediate directions.

verses.text:
तावुभौ क्रूरकर्माणावुभौ भारत दुःसहौ ।
घोररूपमयुध्येतां कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ ।
त्रासयन्तौ जगत्सर्वं ज्याक्षेपविहतत्वचौ ॥

meaning.en: Both were cruel in action and both hard to bear, O Bharata; each wishing to repay the other's blows, they fought a terrible fight, terrifying the whole world as their bowstrings flayed their forearms.

verses.text:
शकुनिस्तु रणे वीरो युधिष्ठिरमपीडयत् ।
तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा सुबलस्य सुतो विभुः ।
नादं चकार बलवान्सर्वसैन्यानि कम्पयन् ॥

meaning.en: In the battle the hero Shakuni tormented Yudhishthira. Having killed his four horses, the mighty son of Subala roared, shaking all the armies.

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरं राजानमपराजितम् ।
अपोवाह रथेनाजौ सहदेवः प्रतापवान् ॥

meaning.en: Meanwhile the valiant Sahadeva carried the hero, the undefeated king, away from the battle in his chariot.

verses.text:
अथान्यं रथमास्थाय धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः ।
शकुनिं नवभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध पञ्चभिः ।
ननाद च महानादं प्रवरः सर्वधन्विनाम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the righteous king Yudhishthira, mounting another chariot, pierced Shakuni with nine arrows and again with five, and gave a great roar, that best of all archers.

verses.text:
तद्युद्धमभवच्चित्रं घोररूपं च मारिष ।
ईक्षितृप्रीतिजननं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् ॥

meaning.en: That fight, O revered one, was wondrous and terrible, delighting the onlookers and attended by Siddhas and Charanas.

verses.text:
उलूकस्तु महेष्वासं नकुलं युद्धदुर्मदम् ।
अभ्यद्रवदमेयात्मा शरवर्षैः समन्ततः ॥

meaning.en: But Uluka, of immeasurable spirit, rushed on all sides with showers of arrows at the great archer Nakula, who was wild for battle.

verses.text:
तथैव नकुलः शूरः सौबलस्य सुतं रणे ।
शरवर्षेण महता समन्तात्पर्यवारयत् ॥

meaning.en: In the same way the brave Nakula surrounded Shakuni's son in the battle on every side with a great shower of arrows.

verses.text:
तौ तत्र समरे वीरौ कुलपुत्रौ महारथौ ।
योधयन्तावपश्येतां परस्परकृतागसौ ॥

meaning.en: In that fight the two heroes, great chariot-fighters of noble houses, each guilty of wrongs against the other, were seen battling.

verses.text:
तथैव कृतवर्मा तु शैनेयं शत्रुतापनम् ।
योधयञ्शुशुभे राजन्बलं शक्र इवाहवे ॥

meaning.en: So too Kritavarman, fighting the scorcher of foes, Satyaki, shone in the battle like Shakra at the head of his force, O king.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनो धनुश्छित्त्वा धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे ।
अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: Duryodhana cut Dhrishtadyumna's bow in the encounter and then pierced him, bowless, with sharp arrows.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि समरे प्रगृह्य परमायुधम् ।
राजानं योधयामास पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम् ॥

meaning.en: Dhrishtadyumna too, taking up a superb weapon, fought the king while all the archers looked on.

verses.text:
तयोर्युद्धं महच्चासीत्संग्रामे भरतर्षभ ।
प्रभिन्नयोर्यथा सक्तं मत्तयोर्वरहस्तिनोः ॥

meaning.en: Great was their battle, O bull of the Bharatas, like the clash of two choice elephants in rut, their temples split.

verses.text:
गौतमस्तु रणे क्रुद्धो द्रौपदेयान्महाबलान् ।
विव्याध बहुभिः शूरः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ॥

meaning.en: Meanwhile Gautama Kripa, angry in the battle, the hero, pierced the mighty sons of Draupadi with many straight-jointed arrows.

verses.text:
तस्य तैरभवद्युद्धमिन्द्रियैरिव देहिनः ।
घोररूपमसंवार्यं निर्मर्यादमतीव च ॥

meaning.en: His fight with them was like that of an embodied soul with the senses: terrible, unstoppable and wholly without restraint.

verses.text:
ते च तं पीडयामासुरिन्द्रियाणीव बालिशम् ।
स च तान्प्रतिसंरब्धः प्रत्ययोधयदाहवे ॥

meaning.en: They pressed him hard as the senses press a fool, and he, enraged, fought them back in the battle.

verses.text:
एवं चित्रमभूद्युद्धं तस्य तैः सह भारत ।
उत्थायोत्थाय हि यथा देहिनामिन्द्रियैर्विभो ॥

meaning.en: So, O Bharata, his battle with them was strange, as the senses rise again and again against an embodied soul, O lord.

verses.text:
नराश्चैव नरैः सार्धं दन्तिनो दन्तिभिस्तथा ।
हया हयैः समासक्ता रथिनो रथिभिस्तथा ।
संकुलं चाभवद्भूयो घोररूपं विशां पते ॥

meaning.en: Men were locked with men, elephants with elephants, horses with horses and chariot-fighters with chariot-fighters, and the press grew ever more terrible, O lord of the people.

verses.text:
इदं चित्रमिदं घोरमिदं रौद्रमिति प्रभो ।
युद्धान्यासन्महाराज घोराणि च बहूनि च ॥

meaning.en: This was strange, this dreadful, this fierce, O lord: many were the fights, and all of them terrible, O great king.

verses.text:
ते समासाद्य समरे परस्परमरिंदमाः ।
विव्यधुश्चैव जघ्नुश्च समासाद्य महाहवे ॥

meaning.en: Meeting one another in the battle, those subduers of foes pierced and slew each other in the great fray.

verses.text:
तेषां शस्त्रसमुद्भूतं रजस्तीव्रमदृश्यत ।
प्रवातेनोद्धतं राजन्धावद्भिश्चाश्वसादिभिः ॥

meaning.en: A thick dust, raised by their weapons, was seen, stirred by the wind and by horsemen racing about, O king.

verses.text:
रथनेमिसमुद्भूतं निःश्वासैश्चापि दन्तिनाम् ।
रजः संध्याभ्रकपिलं दिवाकरपथं ययौ ॥

meaning.en: Dust thrown up by chariot wheels and by the breath of elephants, tawny as an evening cloud, rose to the path of the sun.

verses.text:
रजसा तेन संपृक्ते भास्करे निष्प्रभीकृते ।
संछादिताभवद्भूमिस्ते च शूरा महारथाः ॥

meaning.en: With the sun mingled with that dust and robbed of its light, the earth was covered over, as were those brave great chariot-fighters.

verses.text:
मुहूर्तादिव संवृत्तं नीरजस्कं समन्ततः ।
वीरशोणितसिक्तायां भूमौ भरतसत्तम ।
उपाशाम्यत्ततस्तीव्रं तद्रजो घोरदर्शनम् ॥

meaning.en: In a moment all around became free of dust, for on the ground, soaked with the blood of heroes, that fearsome dust settled, O best of the Bharatas.

verses.text:
ततोऽपश्यं महाराज द्वंद्वयुद्धानि भारत ।
यथाप्राग्र्यं यथाज्येष्ठं मध्याह्ने वै सुदारुणे ।
वर्मणां तत्र राजेन्द्र व्यदृश्यन्तोज्ज्वलाः प्रभाः ॥

meaning.en: Then, O great king, I saw duels in the dreadful midday, pairing each by rank and age; and the bright gleams of the armor were seen there, O king of kings.

verses.text:
शब्दः सुतुमुलः संख्ये शराणां पततामभूत् ।
महावेणुवनस्येव दह्यमानस्य सर्वतः ॥

meaning.en: A great tumult arose in the battle from the falling arrows, like the sound of a vast bamboo forest burning on every side.
